articles.title: Steve Kornacki explains 'abrupt ending' to epic midterm marathon stream
articles.summary: Steve Kornacki is explaining why he dipped out of his marathon midterms stream without saying goodbye: "Things caught up to me in a hurry at hour 10."
articles.body:
Steve Kornacki is back to give viewers some closure after his epic midterms marathon.

The network's chief data analyst went live for a whopping 10 straight hours for NBC News' coverage of the midterm elections Nov. 3. Throughout the evening, Kornacki regularly appeared on the NBC television network to discuss the election results as they came in. But NBC also hosted a " Kornacki Cam " livestream that stayed with Kornacki all night long.

The stream ended a bit abruptly, though: After impressively staying on for more than 10 hours with virtually no breaks, Kornacki told viewers he'd be taking five minutes and would be "right back," only to never return.

In an early morning X post on Nov. 4 , Kornacki explained he had planned to be live for 13 hours but had to dip out a bit earlier than anticipated.

"I was sure 13 hours would be fine but things caught up to me in a hurry at hour 10," he wrote. "I can't say thanks enough to all of you. What a ride and I think we did make livestream history. Sorry for the abrupt ending!"

Prior to Kornacki's update, viewers had joked about the lack of closure to the stream: "I didn't want him to go without saying goodbye," one person wrote in the YouTube comments, while another quipped, "I'm not going to bed until there is proof of life from Steve."

At the start of Kornacki's coverage, which officially kicked off about 30 minutes before the first polls closed, the elections guru told viewers he was embarking on a "grand livestream experiment." All night, the stream would show Kornacki whenever he joined the NBC network for analysis. But in between those segments, the stream would keep on rolling continuously, so Kornacki would continue talking to viewers and providing insights.

"We're doing something we've never done before," he said, explaining, "I'm going to be going into the NBC broadcast. You'll see that on this livestream. I'm going to be coming back when I'm not on NBC, and we're going to be doing results, results, results. We're going to do it all night."

NBC previously utilized the "Kornacki Cam" numerous times during primary election coverage, though prior streams were typically not as lengthy or elaborate as the midterm marathon. "This started as an experiment with a House special election last year and turned into this," Kornacki wrote on X .

In March, Kornacki told The Hollywood Reporter that his "Kornacki Cam" streams allow him to provide the viewer with "a much more kind of comprehensive picture of how the election was won or lost."

Kornacki noted at the start that he was skeptical of how it would work to do a stream in the same studio where NBC anchors Savannah Guthrie and Tom Llamas would be hosting the network's regular election coverage.

"When they told me they wanted to try this, I was like, 'Well, Savannah and Tom are going to want to kill me because I'm going to drive them crazy,'" he said. "But we tested the sound and everything. They said they don't really hear me. I don't really hear them."

Kornacki, famed for providing incisive election analysis and breaking down results by county while standing in front of a screen dubbed the Big Board, also said early on that his plan was to keep streaming "through the morning."

As the stream continued, viewers in the live chat and on social media marveled at Kornacki's stamina, especially considering he was standing the entire time and was rarely off camera for more than a few moments. Even when he wasn't speaking, the feed would usually still show Kornacki looking at his phone or a nearby monitor.

"Steve's multitasking skills is legendary," one viewer commented in the live chat, and YouTuber David Doel praised the stream as possibly the "greatest thing NBC has ever concocted."

At one point, after nine hours of coverage, NBC anchor Craig Melvin addressed viewers who might be confused about how Kornacki was still going. "For those of you who might be concerned about Steve Kornacki's well-being … I can confirm that Steve Kornacki has had a bathroom break, and we are nourishing him, as well."

According to NBC, the "Kornacki Cam" stream was the No. 1 election live stream on YouTube for the midterms, and it amassed 29 million views across platforms.

articles.title: Google derruba esquema que controlava 1 milhão de aparelhos infectados; Brasil é o 2º mais afetado | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a empresa, fabricante chinesa instalava programa malicioso de fábrica e vendia acesso aos dispositivos para criminosos. Maioria dos equipamentos era de TV boxes com Android.
articles.summary: Segundo a empresa, fabricante chinesa instalava programa malicioso de fábrica e vendia acesso aos dispositivos para criminosos. Maioria dos equipamentos era de TV boxes com Android.
articles.body:
Google derruba rede com 1,3 milhão de aparelhos infectados, incluindo TV boxes; Brasil é o 2º mais afetado — Foto: Reprodução/Google

Uma operação do Google com outras empresas de tecnologia desmantelou uma rede que controlava mais de 1,3 milhão de aparelhos sem o conhecimento dos donos. Os dispositivos tinham um programa malicioso chamado XCPE, instalado de fábrica. A maioria era de TV boxes com Android .

O Brasil foi o segundo país com mais dispositivos afetados , atrás apenas da Malásia, segundo a empresa de cibersegurança Trend Micro. Foram identificados aparelhos infectados em 170 países. Iraque, México e Taiwan também estão entre os mais atingidos.

Segundo o Google, a fabricante Videostrong, sediada em Shenzhen, na China, instalou intencionalmente o programa no sistema dos equipamentos. A infecção não dependia de o usuário clicar em um link suspeito: os aparelhos já saíam de fábrica com o vírus.

A fabricante ganhava dinheiro vendendo a criminosos o acesso aos aparelhos infectados . Eles usavam os dispositivos para simular visualizações de anúncios e gerar receita com publicidade.

Embora a maioria dos aparelhos infectados fosse de TV boxes, o Google também identificou o programa em dispositivos de telemedicina, máquinas de karaokê e equipamentos de sinalização digital.

Fabricantes podem firmar contratos com o Google para oferecer serviços da empresa em seus aparelhos, como o Android TV. Segundo o Google, essas empresas precisam cumprir requisitos e passar por testes de compatibilidade e segurança.

A Videostrong, porém, usou técnicas para esconder o programa e burlar essas verificações, afirmou o Google. Isso permitia carregar código malicioso após o aparelho ser ligado pela primeira vez .

Segundo a empresa, a Videostrong adotava essa prática desde o fim de 2024.

"Um fabricante de dispositivos infectar intencionalmente seus usuários com malware é uma quebra inaceitável de confiança e representa um risco sério para esses usuários", disse o Google.

A empresa informou que rompeu relações com a Videostrong e proibiu ela de produzir e vender aparelhos Android certificados ou fornecer software a outros fabricantes certificados. Também afirmou que alterou seu processo de revisão para proteger os consumidores.

Aparelho de TV Box da Videostrong — Foto: Reprodução/Videostrong

Procurada pelo g1 , a Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) afirmou que combate a venda de produtos não homologados devido aos riscos para os consumidores e para as redes de telecomunicações.

"O impacto da utilização de equipamentos não homologados vai muito além das questões de qualidade do serviço fornecido ao consumidor ou da segurança física do aparelho. Trata-se de uma ameaça direta à infraestrutura cibernética do país", afirmou ao g1 Gesiléa Fonseca Teles, superintendente de fiscalização da agência.

"A proteção das telecomunicações exige vigilância constante, cooperação institucional e a conscientização de que a integridade da rede depende da procedência e conformidade do hardware conectado", completou.

A Anatel não participou da operação. Segundo o Google, a ação envolveu a Agência Nacional de Polícia do Japão e as empresas Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient e TrendAI.

articles.title: An excellent breakdown of what dial-up modems were saying to each other.
articles.summary:

articles.title: Indira Krishna recalls first cast reading session of 'Ramayana' with Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi; says 'From Animal to Ramayana I witnessed this pure soul actor'
articles.summary: Television actress Indira Krishna, who will be seen in Bollywood's mythological saga Ramayana as Mata Kaushalya, recalled her first day with the Ramayana
articles.body: Television actress Indira Krishna, who will be seen in Bollywood's mythological saga Ramayana as Mata Kaushalya, recalled her first day with the Ramayana cast. She took a trip down memory lane and recalled the first day of the cast reading session for Nitesh Tiwari's much-anticipated film 'Ramayana', featuring Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi in the lead roles.She took to her social media account to share a series of pictures from the memorable day. Indira expressed nostalgia and penned heartfelt notes for her co-stars and the film's team. She praised Ranbir Kapoor with whom she has shared screen space in two films, 'Animal' and 'Ramayana'.Praising Ranbir, she said she witnessed the actor's journey from 'Animal' to 'Ramayana' and described him as a beautiful person both inside and out. She also lauded his performance and said he nailed his role.Sharing her memories, Indira wrote, "Our first day of cast reading session. What a memorable day and today I could feel this nostalgia. RK I hv no words to tell how beautiful inside out u are. From Animal to Ramayana I witnessed this pure soul actor and believe me he nailed it. Take a bow RK."Talking about Sai Pallavi, who plays Goddess Sita, Indira praised her innocence and spiritual thoughts. She added that their coming together for the film seemed destined. She also expressed gratitude towards Ravi for looking after her during their time in Chandigarh and described him as a sweetheart.She added, “Sai ur innocence speaks volumes and ur spiritual thought has brought u to this platform ..ur right we all were destined to meet here.”She went on to praise director Nitesh Tiwari and said she was impressed by the way he guided the cast to bring out the emotions in their performances. She recalled a particular scene before the Vanvas sequence and shared she still remembered how the filmmaker helped her get the shot right in one take.She further praised Rakul Preet Singh for her politeness and cheerful nature and appreciated her portrayal of Surpanakha. Indira went on to thank casting director Mukesh Chhabra for knowing the right cast from the very beginning. She also acknowledged Jay Kar's work and recalled experiencing an elaborate camera setup involving more than 80 cameras.While concluding her note, the actress expressed love and gratitude to the entire team and wrote, "Love u all ..cheers to the team cheers to Namit Malhotra's Ramayana..JAI SHREE RAM."Indira Krishnan plays Mata Kaushalya, the mother of Lord Ram (played by Ranbir Kapoor), in Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana.’'Ramayana' is slated to hit theatres today, November 5, 2026, across India.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: Where is Windows 12?
articles.summary: Microsoft seems happy to stick with Windows 11, for now.﻿
articles.body: While I wasn’t expecting Microsoft to announce Windows 12 during its RTX Spark launch event last month, more than a few people were hoping to see something truly new. Between the growing frustration with Windows 11 and the muted response to Copilot Plus PCs, it’s starting to feel like Microsoft needs to go bigger with its desktop OS. Much of this year’s Windows development has been focused on underlying performance improvements, after Microsoft acknowledged the bloat and reliability issues with Windows 11 and created a plan to fix them. That work is ongoing, and sources tell me there’s now a big focus on quality for the next major release of Windows 11 in 2027. Microsoft started planning to shift back to a three-year release cycle for Windows in 2022, with the first big release in 2024. At the time, many expected that to be Windows 12, but the company stuck to a major update of Windows 11 instead. Now that the three-year cycle is about to hit again, it looks like Microsoft is promising to improve Windows 11 instead of rolling new features and underlying improvements into a Windows 12 release. Sources tell me that Microsoft is already preparing for Windows 11 version 27H2. Like the big 24H2 release in 2024, this will be a full OS swap, where Microsoft replaces or upgrades major parts of the OS. The past couple of annual releases (25H2 and 26H2) have been enablement packages, which simply switch new features on gradually as they’re rolled out in monthly cumulative updates. Since this is a bigger release, more testing will be required for the new features and changes that Microsoft is planning to make next year. We will likely see Windows Insider testing begin a lot sooner than the typical June timeframe Microsoft used for both 25H2 and 26H2. Microsoft is also preparing for the big release of Windows 11 next year by replacing the default wallpaper of the operating system. Sources tell me a new wallpaper will be unveiled at Microsoft’s Ignite conference later this month, with a series of designs replacing Bloom, the current default. Microsoft used Bloom to market Windows 11 heavily during its launch phase, with “Bloomberry” ice cream and the wallpaper gracing the famous Times Square screens. [Image: One of the new Windows 11 wallpapers. The wallpaper replacements will vary across consumer and commercial versions of Windows 11, I’m told. The designs are similar to Bloom, but with a folding sheet of color immersed in clouds. The Windows 11 Pro version looks the most like the Bloom colors, while there are subtle variations for the consumer versions of Windows 11, focused on gaming, productivity, creator, and performance. Microsoft has quietly started using some of these new wallpapers in its recent Windows 11 marketing materials, and it plans to preview the full Bloom replacement at Ignite before rolling it out broadly in early January. The question I can’t answer yet is whether Microsoft will even consider moving to Windows 12 branding next year, or whether that’s still a few years away. Microsoft seems to be set on improving Windows 11’s reputation, but it’s a difficult task to achieve when lots of people have already made their minds up. Even Microsoft’s performance improvements haven’t convinced everyone yet. Microsoft showed off some more of its memory optimization work earlier this week, improving performance and multitasking on PCs with 8GB of RAM. “Windows can now keep up to 2 GB more of your active data in memory instead of moving it to slower storage, so an app or tab you left open is less likely to reload when you return,” explains Windows chief Pavan Davuluri. I’ve seen YouTubers and even some Windows Insiders question this work, skeptical that Microsoft is actually making improvements. But it’s not just a false promise from Windows engineers; there’s a big effort to make a series of small improvements that all add up to a better performance across a variety of hardware. Windows Central tested Microsoft’s claims and found that the latest updates to Windows 11 do, in fact, improve memory usage. Paging less data to disk will also improve performance, particularly when you’re multitasking between apps on a system with just 8GB of RAM. Microsoft is making improvements to memory usage in apps like Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook, too, so this isn’t even just a Windows effort anymore. These changes are hard to notice unless you compare two systems side by side, and Microsoft clearly has a perception problem with Windows 11 that steady improvements like this won’t overcome. Microsoft ultimately missed a chance to simply own up to the malware-like ads it has squeezed into Windows 11 and be transparent about the fact that they were a mistake. Instead, I think the company is betting that it can win back users over the long term through genuine improvements rather than a marketing exercise that packages everything up into a shiny, new Windows 12 release. Whether that’s enough to change how people feel about Windows remains to be seen, but Microsoft needs to give people a reason to be excited about Windows again, not just another reason to tolerate it. The pad * The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic are all promising to adopt a new standard that will allow publishers to opt out of being scraped by AI bots. As Google Zero continues to reshape the publishing industry, Microsoft says websites will still appear in Bing’s search results even if AI training has been blocked. Anthropic has already adopted this new signal, which is part of a website’s robots.txt file, and Google and Microsoft are both planning to support it next year. * Curry Barker used a Surface Laptop Ultra to help make his new YouTube short. Microsoft is promoting the performance benefits of RTX Spark on battery by showcasing that Obsession director Curry Barker used a Surface Laptop Ultra to edit the full Mama Bear film while unplugged. The edit obviously wasn’t performed on a single battery charge, as Microsoft notes, but it’s more to point out that Windows laptops have finally caught up to the MacBook Pro’s ability to maintain near-identical performance whether on battery or plugged in. * Windows 11 tries new shortcuts for Xbox gaming mode and search. Microsoft has started testing new Windows 11 builds that improve on the recently refreshed Windows Search and add quick settings to Xbox mode. Windows Insiders can now test out filters in search for files, actions, or web results, as well as perform actions like changing screen brightness or volume. The Xbox mode in Windows 11 is also getting quick settings to easily toggle things like Bluetooth and Wi-Fi without having to exit to the desktop mode on a handheld gaming PC. * Xbox’s former COO has “serious concerns” about her abrupt departure. I said this was weird last week. Xbox’s former chief operating officer, Helen Chiang, suddenly left Microsoft less than two weeks ago after being promoted into the role in July. A surprisingly short memo from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed the news internally, and now Chiang says she has “serious concerns” about how she was treated. In a lengthy post on LinkedIn, Chiang doesn’t dispute she was fired but says a Eurogamer report that it was related to policy violations is “not accurate.” Chiang also denies unfounded rumors that speculated she was leaking information, or that she left to join a competitor. I’ve only heard really positive things about Chiang, so this whole turn of events is very puzzling. * The Elder Scrolls VI officially has a name: Sentinel. I reported in Notepad last week that Sentinel would be the official subtitle of The Elder Scrolls VI, and Bethesda confirmed it this week with a brief teaser video. While the game is still at least two years away from release, Bethesda has been showing off some parts of the story internally in recent months. There have been many leaks about The Elder Scrolls VI in recent years, and I will say that one was very accurate, while many others have been far off the mark. * Xbox’s smallest-ever controller is surprisingly comfortable. I’ve been testing out the new $49.99 Xbox Nano controller over the past few days, and I’m impressed with the design. I have small hands so it’s perfectly suited to me, and it’s designed for younger people and gaming on the go. The big difference with the Nano over regular Xbox controllers is the size of the triggers. They’re also a lot more clicky than the thud on the regular controller. The battery life is also something you’ll have to get used to, as it seems to drain fully in around five to six hours. * Xbox’s Arkane Studios attracts multiple bidders, including Ubisoft. We’re just weeks away from hearing about the fate of Blade developers Arkane Studios, and it looks like Microsoft has some options lined up for the studio. Bloomberg reports that Ubisoft and “at least two other gaming companies” have made bids for Arkane. Microsoft is also considering selling the studio to its management. I wrote last week that “I’m cautiously optimistic that Blade will be saved.” * Microsoft is improving Outlook search with a small language model. Microsoft has heard the feedback about Outlook search and it’s looking to improve result ranking, results when connectivity is poor, and a better feedback loop for end users. Classic Outlook will now automatically fall back to a local index when connectivity to cloud servers is poor. This should improve the speed of results, but Microsoft is also using an Outlook-specific small language model ranker to improve the relevancy and speed of results. You’ll also be able to use a thumbs up or down on Outlook search results to let Microsoft know how happy you are with the changes. * The new Windows 11 speed test was built by an AI agent. Microsoft saw the feedback about the taskbar speed test throwing you to a webpage, and it designed a fully integrated version for Windows 11 instead. “The design and build work was driven by an agentic AI workflow, with a person guiding the process in their spare time,” says Marcus Ash, head of design and research for Windows and devices. It took only a day to get a working prototype ready. “This is where I see a lot of potential in AI,” says Ash. “Getting from idea to customer value faster. Without AI slop. That is the way.” * Xbox previews two new ways to control cloud games. Microsoft’s new Xbox Nano controller now supports a Wi-Fi connection directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming, just like Google’s Stadia controllers. It was a hidden feature when I tried out the new controller recently, and US players will be able to preview it ahead of a broader rollout. Microsoft is also previewing a new phone controller option for playing cloud games on smart TVs. * Xbox overhauls its PC, web, and cloud apps with a faster design. Microsoft is unveiling a new Xbox PC app today that launches “up to 60 percent faster” than before, with an overhauled design to match new updates to Xbox Cloud Gaming on the web and smart TVs. Xbox Insiders will be able to start testing the updated Xbox PC app today, and the updated Xbox Cloud Gaming interface will start rolling out over the next few weeks. I’ve been trying out the new Xbox PC app on the Xbox Ally X handheld in recent weeks, and it’s noticeably faster and feels much more like I’m navigating an Xbox console interface than before. It’s good to see these much-needed improvements for the Xbox PC app. I’m always keen to hear from readers, so please drop a comment here, or you can reach me at notepad@theverge.com if you want to discuss anything else. If you’ve heard about any of Microsoft’s secret projects, you can reach me via email at notepad@theverge.com or speak to me confidentially on the Signal messaging app, where I’m tomwarren.01. I’m also tomwarren on Telegram, if you’d prefer to chat there. Thanks for subscribing to Notepad.

articles.title: Ember’s smallest self-heating mug is on sale for just $33
articles.summary: The six-ounce Ember Cup is on sale for $32.99 ($67 off) at Woot until November 8th, making it a more affordable alternative to the company’s pricier smart mugs.
articles.body: We’ve been fans of Ember’s temperature-controlled mugs for years, though given the price tag, we admit that they’re somewhat of a luxury purchase. Thankfully, if you’ve been looking for a more affordable option, Woot is selling the Ember Cup in black for $32.99 ($67 off) with a 90-day warranty through November 7th. You can potentially save even more as part of Woot’s larger Home and Kitchen Sale, which lets you save an additional $20 off orders of $100 or more when you use code COOK at checkout. [Product: Ember Cup (six-ounce) | Granted, six ounces isn’t much, but the smaller, handle-free cup is well-suited for cappuccinos, cortados, flat whites, and other espresso-based drinks. It’s also a perfectly fine option if you don’t mind refilling your cup of coffee, cocoa, or tea throughout the day. I’m actually tempted to pick one up myself at this price, especially since I’ve been trying (with varying degrees of success) to cut back on coffee. Like Ember’s larger mugs, the smart cup lets you choose and set your drinking temperature between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit using a companion app, then remembers your setting for future drinks. It can then maintain that temperature for up to 95 minutes on a charge, up to four hours with a lid, or even all day if you leave it on the included charging dock. The cup also automatically enters sleep mode after two hours of inactivity to conserve power. Just keep in mind that, despite its IPX7 water-resistance rating, the cup is hand-wash only.

articles.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is $300 off ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: In addition to the discounted folding phone, today’s best deals include Lego Chopper, the droid from Ahsoka, a 2K Ring video doorbell, and the Beats Pill.
articles.body: Android fans with a bit of iPhone Duo envy, take note: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is discounted to $1,599.99 at both Amazon and Best Buy, a hefty $300 markdown from its usual price, and just $50 higher than the lowest we’ve seen. Considering the device only launched a few months ago, you’re saving a significant amount of cash on the unlocked device, and you can also opt for the 512GB model, doubling the storage, for just $200 more (Amazon, Best Buy). Best Buy currently has all three colors in stock, while the 256GB model is currently sold out on Amazon in cream. [Product: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 | The shorter and wider passport-style shape (similar to the iPhone Duo) quickly became natural and comfortable to handle, according to our reviewer Dominic Preston’s experience with the Z Fold 8. Despite its thin and light construction, it doesn’t skimp on battery life, with a 4,800mAh battery that still had 40 percent charge remaining after a full day of use. The interior 4:3 screen has the same ratio as most Apple iPads, which is great for watching movies or TV, but even better for reading. There’s no telephoto lens on this model (it’s present on the pricier Z Fold 8 Ultra), and it only has an IP48 rating, so you’ll want to be careful near the beach, but those are small compromises to make given the discounted price. Read our Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 review. Other deals to consider * Both Amazon and Best Buy are selling the Beats Pill for a discounted $99.95 and $99.99 respectively, a sizable break from the usual $149.99 price point. The 2024 edition of this iconic Bluetooth speaker adds in lossless audio over USB-C, as well as native feature support for both iOS and Android devices. It’s rated IP67 for dust and water resistance, and comes in three different colors to match your other Beats devices. Read our review. * The Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is on sale for $39.99 at Amazon, over half off its $99.99 list price. This battery-powered doorbell camera is easy to install, and shoots clear 2K resolution video with a 140-degree field of view and up to 6X digital zoom. You’ll get real-time notifications on your phone for any activity the camera spots, with live view and two-way talk in case you need to have a chat with your neighbors or delivery folks without coming to the front door. * You can pick up the Lego Star Wars: Ahsoka Chopper set for just $66.99 at Amazon, the lowest price we’ve seen yet for this 1,039-piece building kit. This brick-based droid has great play features, like detachable arms and center wheel for different display positions, and a head that spins and bobs realistically. It stands at over 8.5 inches when fully built, making it a fun addition to your existing Lego display or bookshelf.

articles.title: Vizio told us it doesn’t ignore ACR opt-outs.
articles.summary:
While a Northeastern study showed a Vizio TV sending data to suspected ACR endpoints even after opt-out, Vizio spokesperson Mischa Dunton told The Verge via email, “The encrypted traffic researchers observed is not ACR data, but rather routine operational data used to support the Vizio experience.”
[Link: Maybe your TV won’t stop spying on you | https://www.theverge.com/tech/1026088/northeastern-university-acr-tracking-study | The Verge]
articles.body:
While a Northeastern study showed a Vizio TV sending data to suspected ACR endpoints even after opt-out, Vizio spokesperson Mischa Dunton told The Verge via email, “The encrypted traffic researchers observed is not ACR data, but rather routine operational data used to support the Vizio experience.”

articles.title: Meta is delaying its controversial new business terms indefinitely.
articles.summary:
The new terms had come under scrutiny over language that appeared to give Meta broad leeway to train AI on scraped publisher content, even after the company updated them.
Meta said last week it expected to delay implementation past November 20th (which itself was a delayed date). Now, Meta states on its website that the new terms “will not take effect on November 20, 2026,” as reported by Nieman Lab.

articles.title: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15: Farrhana Bhatt reveals suffering heavy bleeding and severe cramps after helicopter stunt; says she could barely stand
articles.summary: Farrhana Bhatt, who emerged as one of the finalists of Khatron Ke Khiladi 15, has opened up about the physical challenges she faced while shooting for the
articles.body: Farrhana Bhatt, who emerged as one of the finalists of Khatron Ke Khiladi 15, has opened up about the physical challenges she faced while shooting for the stunt-based reality show in Cape Town. During an interaction with Hauterrfly on The Male Feminist episode, Farrhana recalled how the first stunt of the season turned into a frightening experience for her.Farrhana shared that her condition worsened after she returned to her hotel. Recalling the experience, she said, “After that I went to my hotel and I haven’t had cramps like that in my entire life. I could not even stand, I froze.” She added that she contacted her gynaecologist, who attributed the symptoms to stress and the sudden physical and emotional pressure her body had experienced.The actor also revealed that she was worried about how she would manage the next day’s stunt while dealing with such severe pain. According to Farrhana, this was the first time she had to rely on painkillers to get through the demanding schedule. She disclosed that she was taking two painkillers every day during that period.Farrhana further explained that the problem did not end with the shoot in South Africa. When she returned to India, she experienced the same bleeding again after three months. She consulted her doctor once more and was reportedly told that stress could be responsible for the symptoms.Speaking about how difficult the experience was, Farrhana said, “I can’t even explain the pain. I did not tell anyone about this, it is just my habit that even when something happens, I keep it to myself.” She also spoke about experiencing anxiety attacks while participating in Bigg Boss, revealing another aspect of the emotional challenges she has faced during reality television appearances.Farrhana Bhatt on taking a break from adventure-based reality showsIn September, Farrhana had spoken about wanting to step away from physically and emotionally challenging reality shows for some time after her experience on Khatron Ke Khiladi 15. She also clarified that she would not be joining the upcoming season of Roadies as a gang leader.More about Khatron Ke Khiladi 15Hosted by filmmaker Rohit Shetty, Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 returned to television after a two-year break. The season featured several popular television and entertainment personalities competing in challenging stunts involving heights, water, animals and other fear-based tasks.Avinash emerged as the winner of the season, while Rithvik Dhanjani and Orhan Awatramani, popularly known as Orry, secured the first and second runner-up positions, respectively.The contestant lineup included Rubina Dilaik, Jasmin Bhasin, Karan Wahi, Rithvik Dhanjani, Vishal Aditya Singh, Shagun Sharma, Avika Gor, Avinash Mishra, Harsh Gujral and Ruhaanika Dhawan, among others.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more.
